subsystems.name: Display engine
subsystems.role: creates the tiny, very bright image that gets projected into the eye.

subsystems.name: Waveguide combiner
subsystems.role: carries the image across the lens and releases it toward the pupil while still letting real light through.

subsystems.name: Sensing and tracking
subsystems.role: works out where the head, hands and surroundings are so overlays stay anchored.

subsystems.name: Compute, wireless and power
subsystems.role: runs the software and links to a phone or cloud when the onboard chip is not enough.

subsystems.name: Frame and ergonomics
subsystems.role: keeps the whole stack light enough and cool enough to wear all day.

subsystems.name: Audio and interaction
subsystems.role: lets the wearer control the device without a screen or keyboard.

buildSteps.title: Design the optical stack
buildSteps.detail: Modelling sets the field of view, the size of the eye box and the colour performance before any glass is cut.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the waveguide
buildSteps.detail: Micro- or nano-scale gratings are patterned onto a glass or polymer wafer by etching or nanoimprint, then the wafer is diced and polished into individual lenses.

buildSteps.title: Make the microdisplay
buildSteps.detail: Micro-LED arrays are grown and transferred onto a silicon backplane, or an LCoS panel is built, giving a panel only a few millimetres across.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the light engine
buildSteps.detail: The panel, illumination and relay optics are aligned to sub-micron tolerance and bonded into a module.

buildSteps.title: Couple display to waveguide
buildSteps.detail: The projector is positioned against the in-coupling grating and fixed so the pupil lands where the eye will be.

buildSteps.title: Integrate electronics
buildSteps.detail: Cameras, IMU, chip, radios and battery are fitted into the temples and connected to the light engine.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate each unit
buildSteps.detail: Every pair is individually calibrated: display alignment and colour, camera intrinsics, eye-tracking maps and vergence.

buildSteps.title: Test and ship
buildSteps.detail: Units are drop-, sweat- and heat-tested, then run through spatial-mapping and overlay accuracy checks before packing.

prerequisites.why: micro-LED panels are bright and efficient enough outdoors, but full-colour versions at consumer yield are still maturing; LCoS is the current fallback.
surface-relief gratings on glass can now be mass-produced and give a thin, see-through combiner.

prerequisites.tech: Real-time spatial mapping (SLAM) on low power
prerequisites.why: phones and headsets already track position and build 3D maps of a room in real time.
all-day wear needs power and heat budgets that current glasses barely meet, so heavy work is often offloaded to a phone.

prerequisites.tech: Eye and hand tracking at wearable size
prerequisites.why: reliable input without a controller is needed before overlays feel useful rather than gimmicky.

pathway.milestone: display glasses that show notifications, navigation and translations in a monocular or small overlay
pathway.unlocks: hands-free information for cyclists, travellers and warehouse or field workers.

pathway.milestone: binocular full-colour waveguides with hand and eye tracking in a glasses-like frame
pathway.unlocks: 3D overlays that stay fixed in the world, enabling guided repair, training and gaming.

pathway.milestone: all-day glasses with onboard mapping and a multimodal AI assistant
pathway.unlocks: a device that can answer questions about whatever the wearer is looking at.

pathway.milestone: prescription-ready AR glasses light enough to replace the phone for many tasks
pathway.unlocks: mass adoption and a shift of everyday interfaces from screens to the visual field.
